3. The case of the writ-petitioner (respondent herein ) in the above mentioned writ-petition, in short, was that he was the owner of .0080 acre of land as described in the schedule to the writ-petition and had been possessing the said land by constructing a shop thereon and by doing business there. That the then Zamider gave that land along with some other lands to Mymensingh Bhramma Samaj Committee. in the year 1947 Mymensingh Bhramma Samaj Committee gave settlement of that land to Umed Ali and Umed Ali, after promulgation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, became the owner of the said Land under the government and in the records of right Umed Ali's name was duly recorded. That while Umed Ali thus was owner and possessor of that land he let out the same to monthly tenant Md. Mohsin Uddin. The said tenant became defaulter and Umed Ali then filed Small Causes Case No. 3 of 1979 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh and the suit was decreed on 11.07.1982. On the basis of that decree Execution Case No. 4 of 1982 was instituted and the said tenant was ultimately evicted from that land through court. Umed Ali opened separate holding No. I/B, C.K. Ghose Road, Mymensingh in his name and he was paying municipal taxes. Umed Ali subsequently died in the year 1983 leaving 5 sons and 6 daughters. By amicable partition.among the said heirs of Umed Ali his son H.E.M Afzal Ali got this land in his share. H. E.M. Afzal Ali while was in possession of the said land transferred the same to Mst. MonwaraKhatun by deed of exchange dated 29.08.1991. While Mst. Monwara Khatunwas owning and possessing this land she transferred the said .0080 acre of land to the writ petitioner by a registered heba-bil-ewaz deed dated 08.06.1995 and also delivered possession of the said land to the writ-petitioner. Since then the writ-petitioner has been possessing the said land by doing his business therein the name "pias Electronics". In the BRS record the R.O.R. Plot No. 6389 was transferred to BRS Plot No. 7362 and the BRS record of land has been published in the name of the writ-petitioner under DP Khatian No. 943, Bujarat Khatian No. 7349. That while H.E.M. Afzal Ali being the owner of the property was in possession of the property one Nirmal Kumar Chandra claiming himself Secretary of the Bhramma Samaj Committee, Mymensingh filed Other Class Suit No. 308 of 1987 against H.E.M. Afzal Ali in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Mymensingh for eviction. The said suit was transferred to the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Mymensingh and was renumbered as Other Class Suit No. 52 of 1989 and the suit was then dismissed on contest on 11.10.1989. The plaintiff of that suit then filed Other Class Appeal No. I of 1990 in the Court of District Judge, Mymensingh and the said appeal was transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh, who after hearing both the parties, allowed that appeal and decreed the Other Class Suit No. 52 of 1989 by the judgment and order dated 28.03.2000. The writ-petitioner (the respondent herein) having come to know about the decree filed Other Class Suit No. 49 of 2000 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh for declaration of his title upon the suit property and for further declaration that the decree passed in Other Class Appeal No. 1 of 1990 was not binding upon him. Ultimately that suit was decreed on compromise by the judgment and decree dated 03.02.2008. That after passing of the aforesaid decree the writ petitioner filed and application before the Assistant Commissioner (land) Sadar, Mymensingh for mutation of the land in his name, but the Assistant Commissioner (land) Sadar, Mymensingh did not mutate the land in the name of the petitioner. The writ-petitioner then filed an application before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Mymensingh also for mutation of this land in his name, but did not get any result and thus the writ petitioner was constrained to file the writ petition and obtained rule. 

 7. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides and the facts and circumstances. In this leave petition the leave-petitioners though has stated that the land in question has been enlisted as enemy and vested property, but in support of this case no scrap of paper has been produced before us. It has already been pointed out above that in the writ petition though all these leave-petitioners were made parties, but none of them appeared and made any statements opposing the rule. Moreover, from the case of the writ-petitioner respondent, as narrated above, it appears that the suit property rather has been recorded in the name of one Umed Ali and a separate holding also was opened in the name of Umed Ali. From the stated case of the writ-petitioner-respondent it also appears that previously also some other litigations were initiated in respect of this land and in all those litigations the civil courts examined the respective cases of the contesting parties and adjudicated the disputes between the parties. In none of those civil litigations it was ever alleged from any quarter that the land in question was enlisted as enemy and vested property.
